Here, we reported the improvement of Jclocal in REBa2Cu3O7-d by the increase in ΔSmix at the RE site. Polycrystalline RE123 samples with different ΔSmix were synthesized by solid-state reaction. Through characterization of structural (lattice constants and OP), compositional and superconducting properties (Tc and shielding fraction), seven samples labelled RE-1–RE-7 were chosen, and remanent magnetization measurements were performed on those samples. At higher temperatures (T = 20.0 K), clear difference in Jclocal was not observed. At lower temperatures (T = 2.0 and 4.2 K), higher Jclocal was observed for RE-4 and RE-5 with a higher ΔSmix as compared with that for RE-1, RE-2, and RE-3 with zero or low entropy of mixing at the RE site. Although the results of the current work showed the merit of high-entropy alloying at lower temperatures only, there should be optimal conditions on constituent RE element, mixing ratio and ΔSmix, which will achieve higher Jclocal at higher temperatures as well. If the trial was achieved, the HEA concept can be applied to all RE123 practical materials to additionally improve their critical current properties.

High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are a new type of alloy with five or more chemical elements arranged on a pseudocrystalline lattice. A high mixing-entropy minimizes the Gibbs free-energy and facilitates their crystallization on simple lattice structures, such as body-centered cubic (bcc) structure,,,. Despite the significant amount of compositional disorder, a subset of the HEAs enters a type-II superconducting phase at cryogenic temperatures,. Their large critical fields combined with superior mechanical and thermal properties render HEA promising candidates for materials applications under extreme conditions, for the fabrication of superconducting magnets, and for superconducting devices based on HEA thin films. Ongoing materials synthesis efforts have extended the family of known superconducting HEAs and developed a phenomenological understanding of their properties,. Various analyses of the upper critical field Hc2 and heat capacity measurements as a function of temperature T support a conventional Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer (BCS) pairing mechanism,,, with intermediate-strong coupling. decision.trend: Research on high-entropy alloys has shown promising results in terms of their superconducting properties. Studies have demonstrated that these alloys can exhibit robust zero-resistance superconductivity under pressure and have high critical current densities. The trend suggests that the emergence of superconductivity in high-entropy alloys is governed by the configurational entropy of mixing, which can be increased by substituting different elements at the rare earth site. Additionally, the superconducting properties of high-entropy alloys seem to suffice a Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) description, and they have been found to be single-band isotropic s-wave superconductors in the dirty limit.
decision.unsolved: The exact mechanism by which the configurational entropy of mixing affects the superconducting properties of high-entropy alloys is still not fully understood. Furthermore, the relationship between the elemental composition and the superconducting critical temperature is not well established. More research is needed to fully characterize the superconducting behavior of high-entropy alloys and to explore their potential applications.
decision.why: The next step would be to design a controlled variable experiment to systematically investigate the effect of configurational entropy of mixing on the superconducting properties of high-entropy alloys. This could involve synthesizing a series of alloys with varying levels of configurational entropy and measuring their superconducting critical temperatures and critical current densities. By doing so, researchers can gain a deeper understanding of the relationship between configurational entropy and superconductivity, and potentially identify new high-entropy alloys with optimized superconducting properties.
